He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== As a freshman, Jackson played basketball for Lutheran Northwest High School in [[Rochester Hills, Michigan]]. He moved to Old Redford Academy in [[Detroit]] for his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Isaiah Jackson commits to Kentucky, video highlights 'making it out’ of Pontiac |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2019/11/isaiah-jackson-commits-to-kentucky-video-highlights-making-it-out-of-pontiac.html |website=MLive |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=November 16, 2019}} As a junior, Jackson competed for SPIRE Academy in [[Geneva, Ohio]] alongside [[LaMelo Ball]] and his Old Redford teammate [[Rocket Watts]].{{cite web |last1=Goricki |first1=David |title=Waterford Mott's Isaiah Jackson, a top MSU target, returns as nation's No. 3 power forward |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/06/18/waterford-motts-isaiah-jackson-returns-nations-no-3-power-forward/1493556001/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=June 18, 2019}} He averaged 14.9 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. For his senior season, he transferred to [[Waterford Mott High School]] in [[Waterford Township, Michigan|Waterford, Michigan]].{{cite web |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Finally home, 5-star Isaiah Jackson lifts Waterford Mott basketball to new level |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2019/12/finally-home-5-star-isaiah-jackson-lifts-waterford-mott-basketball-to-new-level.html |website=MLive |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=December 13, 2019}} Jackson averaged 19.1 points, 13 rebounds and 7.7 blocks per game as a senior.{{cite web |last1=Tucker |first1=Kyle |title=His anger channeled, Isaiah Jackson is already turning heads at Kentucky |url=https://theathletic.com/2220466/2020/11/25/his-anger-channeled-isaiah-jackson-is-already-turning-heads-at-kentucky/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=November 25, 2020}} He was named to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] roster.{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=Deb |title=Four UK MBB Signees Selected for Jordan Brand Classic Game |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2020/2/16/mens-basketball-four-uk-mbb-signees-selected-for-jordan-brand-classic-game |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=February 16, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], Jackson committed to playing college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Kentucky Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] at the [[Champions Classic]]. He had the most single-game blocks by a Kentucky player [[Willie Cauley-Stein]] in 2013.{{cite web |title=Kentucky-Kansas Postgame Notes |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2020/12/2/mens-basketball-kentucky-kansas-postgame-notes.aspx |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |access-date=May 9, 2021 |date=December 2, 2020}} As a freshman, Jackson averaged 8.4 points, 6.6 rebounds and an [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]-high 2.6 blocks per game, earning SEC All-Defensive and All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |title=Isaiah Jackson named to SEC All-Freshman and All-Defensive teams |url=https://www.wymt.com/2021/03/09/isaiah-jackson-named-to-sec-all-freshman-and-all-defensive-teams/ |website=[[WYMT-TV]] |access-date=May
